Common Emerging Technology Agent ScaffoldStudent Operating Guide
How to use the frozen Brightspace scaffold with ChatGPT/Codex to build, test, and document specialist agents
MASY1-GC 1800

Assignments 2-8 use one frozen common scaffold. You are not building a new software architecture every week. Your work is to specialize the supplied agent structure for the week's analytical framework, test whether it reasons correctly, improve it, and exercise professional judgment. Target effort: 60-90 minutes; stop at 90 minutes unless instructed otherwise.
1. What You Receive From the Course
A frozen ZIP file in Brightspace: MASY1800_ET_Agent_Scaffold_v1_0.zip. The Brightspace ZIP is the canonical course version; the instructor does not host a GitHub repository.
A fixed common intake contract describing the emerging technology, intended application, organization, adoption posture, constraints, risk/consequence context, management question, and time horizon.
A fixed common output contract that makes all seven specialists comparable and integrable.
Local standard-library Python tools that build a ChatGPT-ready prompt packet and validate the structured response. The reference workflow does not require an OpenAI API account or API key.
The weekly assignment memo, which tells you what specialist expertise to add and what judgment the agent must support.
2. Required Course Toolchain
ChatGPT + Codex + your own GitHub working repository is the supported course path for Assignments 2-8.
ChatGPT: use it to understand the assignment, reason through the weekly framework, critique outputs, generate contrasting test cases, and interpret results.
Codex inside ChatGPT: use it as the coding/development partner to inspect your working scaffold, modify the specialist files, explain changes, debug bounded code, and help run the included scripts.
Your GitHub repository: use it for your working copy and version history. Record the repository, branch, and commit associated with each submitted agent.
Brightspace: use it to obtain the frozen original ZIP and the weekly assignment memo. Keep the original ZIP unchanged.
Important: Do not depend on ChatGPT/Codex being able to fetch an arbitrary GitHub URL. If needed, upload the assignment memo and relevant scaffold files or ZIP directly to ChatGPT/Codex.
3. The Analytical Rule Every Agent Must Preserve
ET generally  ->  ET for the intended application  ->  ET for that application in this organization

The organization does not change the general evidence about the technology. It changes what that evidence means for the application, the acceptable uncertainty, the timing, and the management action. Every specialist must keep those levels distinct.
Common input
What it means
Emerging technology
The ET being evaluated.
Intended application
The specific organizational use being contemplated.
Organization / industry
The organization type, operating environment, users, capabilities, and constraints.
Adoption posture
Aggressive/leading-edge, moderate/fast-follower, conservative/risk-averse, or another justified posture.
Risk / consequence context
Important regulatory, safety, financial, privacy, operational, or reputational consequences.
Management question / time horizon
What management is deciding now and over what period.

Common output: general ET finding; application finding; organization-specific finding; evidence; contrary evidence/limitations; confidence/uncertainty; value and risk implications; bounded management recommendation; and change/monitoring triggers.
4. Weekly Workflow
Download and preserve the original. Download the frozen ZIP from Brightspace and keep that copy unchanged. Unzip a separate working copy.
Create your working repository. Place the working copy in your own GitHub repository. Create an assignment-specific branch or otherwise preserve a clear commit/version record.
Give ChatGPT/Codex the assignment and scaffold. Upload the weekly assignment memo and the working scaffold files it needs. Ask Codex to inspect the structure before changing anything.
Specialize - do not reinvent. Direct Codex to preserve the FROZEN CORE and implement only the specialist analytical logic required by the weekly assignment.
Build the prompt packet. Use the included local script to combine the common scaffold, your specialist instructions, and a test case into a ChatGPT-ready prompt packet.
Run the specialist in ChatGPT. Submit the prompt packet to ChatGPT. Save the returned structured JSON response into your working copy.
Validate and test. Use the included validator, then repeat with contrasting application/organization cases. Save representative inputs and outputs.
Diagnose and revise. Find at least one weak, generic, unsupported, or context-insensitive result. Use ChatGPT/Codex to help diagnose it, then decide what change is warranted.
Commit and submit evidence. Commit the final candidate agent and record the repository, branch, commit, tests, important revision, remaining limitation, and your independent judgment.
Starter Instruction for ChatGPT/Codex

I am building the [NAME OF SPECIALIST AGENT] for MASY1-GC 1800 Emerging Technologies. I have provided the weekly assignment instructions and the frozen Common Emerging Technology Agent Scaffold. Inspect the scaffold first. Preserve the FROZEN CORE, common input schema, and common output schema. Specialize only the student-editable agent files for this week's analytical framework. The agent must distinguish (1) the ET generally, (2) the ET for the intended application, and (3) the ET for that application in the specified organization/adoption posture. Tell me which files you propose to change and why before changing them. Then help me build the prompt packet, run the required contrast tests, diagnose weaknesses, and preserve the final evidence.
5. Testing and Submission Standard
Test at least two materially different contexts; three are preferred when time permits.
Hold the ET constant while changing the application, organizational context, consequence level, or adoption posture enough that some contextual conclusions should change.
Identify one conclusion that appropriately stayed stable and one that appropriately changed.
Preserve at least one failure or weakness and the revision you made in response. Do not change the test merely to make the agent look successful.
Verify consequential current claims using appropriate original sources. ChatGPT output is not evidence by itself.
Submit / preserve
Minimum evidence
Working agent
Specialist files created from the frozen scaffold.
Version record
Your GitHub repository, branch, and commit.
Test record
Primary and contrast cases with representative structured outputs.
Revision evidence
One important weakness and what you changed.
Independent judgment
Whether the agent performs its specialist role adequately and the most important remaining limitation.
AI / verification note
How ChatGPT/Codex materially helped and how consequential claims or technical guidance were checked.

Boundaries: Do not modify FROZEN CORE files unless an assignment explicitly authorizes an architectural change. Do not purchase or configure an OpenAI API account for the standard course workflow. The scaffold intentionally uses ChatGPT as the interactive model runtime and local code only for prompt construction, versioning, and validation.

Week 7 | Assignment 5 - Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
Governing question: How far has this technology and application diffused, what is accelerating or inhibiting diffusion, and what does that stage imply for this organization?

Expected effort: about 60-90 minutes. Stop at 90 minutes unless the instructor explicitly directs otherwise. Use ChatGPT Work and the supplied scaffold to reduce unnecessary mechanical work; preserve unresolved technical issues rather than turning the assignment into an open-ended development exercise. The quality of the evidence and judgment matters more than technical ornamentation or length.
Purpose and Project Connection

Create a specialist agent that applies diffusion theory to current evidence and distinguishes broad technology diffusion from diffusion of the specific application in the relevant industry or peer group.
Professional Charge

Build an agent that uses Rogers' diffusion concepts to assess where an emerging technology stands, why it is or is not spreading, and what the observed pattern implies for the intended application and organization. The agent should inform timing and peer-position judgment without taking over the broader adoption decision assigned to the next specialist.
Required Scaffold and Build Workflow

Build this specialist agent using the frozen MASY1800 Common Emerging Technology Agent Scaffold and the separate course guide, Building the Seven Individual Specialist Agents in ChatGPT Work. Follow that guide for the common procedures for creating the specialist from the frozen template, testing and revising it, completing the Agent Record, checking scaffold integrity, and packaging the completed agent.

For this assignment, your responsibility is to specialize the common scaffold as the Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent described below. Do not redesign the common architecture. Concentrate your effort on the quality of the Rogers diffusion analysis, current evidence, context-sensitive timing interpretation, testing, and professional judgment.
What to Do – What Should the Agent Be Able to Do?
1.  Require the agent to assess relevant adopter categories and the five diffusion characteristics: relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability, and observability.
2.  Distinguish diffusion of the technology generally from diffusion of the proposed application and, where evidence permits, diffusion within the organization's industry or comparable peer group.
3.  Identify change agents, opinion leaders, ecosystem factors, standards, complementary assets, or other forces that appear to accelerate or inhibit diffusion.

4.  Require the organization-specific interpretation to consider whether the organization behaves more like an innovator/early adopter, fast follower, or conservative adopter, without changing the underlying evidence about diffusion stage.

5. Test the completed specialist using the primary and context-contrast procedure defined in the common Individual Agent Building Instructions. Hold the emerging technology constant while changing the application, industry/peer context, or organizational adoption posture enough that the timing implication should differ. Confirm that the general diffusion evidence and broad stage remain appropriately stable while application-level diffusion, peer-position interpretation, timing implications, and bounded management response change for defensible reasons. Use the contrast to expose whether organizational posture is improperly changing the technology's underlying diffusion stage.

6. Identify at least one diffusion claim for which the evidence is too weak, stale, geographically narrow, industry-specific, or otherwise insufficient to support a confident conclusion. Require the agent to qualify or abstain on that claim and state what newer or broader evidence would be needed.
AI Leverage Hints
Ask AI to help map current evidence to Rogers' factors, but ask it to identify where the mapping is speculative rather than observed.

Ask AI to generate a conservative and an aggressive organization considering the same technology and test whether the agent changes timing implications without changing the general diffusion evidence.
Verify claims about adoption rates, installed base, industry use, market share, standards, or recent diffusion signals against dated original sources.
Required Artifacts

1. Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent Package: Submit the completed agent package and Agent Record produced according to the common Individual Agent Building Instructions. The specialist must implement the Rogers adopter-category and five-factor assessment, general/application/industry diffusion distinction, accelerators and inhibitors, organization-specific timing interpretation, primary and contrast tests, one qualified or abstained weak diffusion claim, one preserved failure or weakness, and known limitations.
2. Run the agent on an emerging technology applied to one business/application case. Upload the output report from the agent.

3. Submit a short report of half a page or less stating your independent professional judgment: Where does the technology/application appear to be in its diffusion process, what evidence supports that placement, what factor most accelerates or inhibits diffusion, and what timing implication follows for this organization without yet making the full adoption decision?

4. Submit an AI/verification note. Briefly state how AI materially helped, how consequential factual or methodological guidance was checked, and where you relied on original evidence rather than model memory or generated summaries.

5. Craft Gained (100 words or fewer): State one important thing you discovered through doing this assignment that you did not understand beforehand. Explain what in your analysis, source checking, agent testing, or revision led you to that discovery, and how it will change the way you evaluate emerging technologies or build and use agents next time. Be specific about the change in your professional judgment or method; do not merely summarize what your agent produced or repeat a course concept.
Team Handoff

Bring the completed agent package and Agent Record as required by the common build instructions. Be prepared to identify the broad diffusion-stage judgment, the strongest diffusion signal, the most important accelerator or inhibitor, one application- or industry-specific diffusion difference, the organization-specific timing implication, one weak or qualified diffusion claim, and one caution the Adoption Agent should inherit when the team integrates this expert.

Weekly IndividualProfessional-Practice Assignments
Student Instructions
Building specialist agents that analyze emerging technologies in context and contribute to an integrated management decision-support tool.
MASY1-GC 1800
How the Weekly Individual Assignments Work

These assignments are the individual practice stage of the course's flipped professional studio. You prepare before class, use class discussion and the instructor's craft-centered lecture to sharpen your understanding, then complete a bounded individual assignment. Your work becomes evidence and an independent point of view that you bring to the following team's in-class production session.

Assignment 1 establishes your professional baseline. Assignments 2 through 8 each create one specialist emerging-technology analysis agent. The seven specialist agents are designed to become components of the team's final application-level mixture-of-experts decision-support tool. The objective is not to create seven unrelated chatbots. Each agent has a bounded analytical responsibility, a common contextual intake, a common structured output, and test evidence that makes later integration possible.

The purpose is not to practice every technique introduced in a module. Each assignment gives you one bounded professional task that advances the semester project and requires judgment. You are expected to decide what matters, use appropriate tools to investigate it, verify consequential claims, and reach a defensible conclusion.

Time expectation: Design your work for 60-90 minutes of focused effort. Stop at 90 minutes unless the instructor explicitly directs otherwise. The frozen course scaffold and ChatGPT/Codex are supplied so that you can spend your time on specialist reasoning, testing, evidence, and judgment rather than rebuilding basic agent plumbing. When the time boundary is reached, preserve unresolved questions, limitations, or test failures.
The Recurring Learning Cycle
Prepare: Acquire enough working knowledge before class to understand the week's emerging-technology concept and professional task.
Receive craft: Use the instructor's lecture, examples, and discussion to recognize hype, weak evidence, hidden assumptions, tradeoffs, and consequential judgments.
Build and analyze individually: Create or improve one bounded specialist agent that applies the week's analytical lens.
Test context sensitivity: Determine whether the agent distinguishes the general state of the technology from what that state means for a specific application and organization.
Decide: Reach your own professional conclusion about the agent's analysis and limitations before team discussion.
Synthesize: Bring the agent, evidence, tests, and judgment to the team so competing designs and interpretations can be challenged and integrated.
Accumulate: The seven specialist agents become the expert components of the final team decision-support system.
The Context Rule for Every Specialist Agent

Emerging technologies are not evaluated in a vacuum. The same technology can deserve different conclusions when the contemplated application, organization, risk environment, or adoption posture changes. Every specialist agent in Assignments 2-8 must therefore distinguish three levels of analysis:
ET generally: What is reasonably true about the emerging technology itself on this agent's analytical dimension?
ET for this application: What changes when the technology is considered for the specific intended use?
ET for this application in this organization: What does the combination imply given the organization's industry, capabilities, constraints, risk tolerance, and emerging-technology posture?

The organization does not rewrite the general evidence. A conservative organization does not make a technology less mature, and an aggressive organization does not make it more mature. Organizational context changes the interpretation, timing, acceptable uncertainty, and management action that follow from the general evidence.
Common Context Intake for Assignments 2-8
Input
Required context
Emerging technology
The technology to be analyzed.
Intended application
The specific use case or organizational capability being contemplated.
Organization
The organization or organization type that would employ the technology.
Industry / sector
The relevant operating, competitive, regulatory, or safety environment.
Business need
The problem, opportunity, or decision the application is intended to address.
Users / stakeholders
The people or groups who use, are affected by, govern, or depend on the application.
Adoption posture
Aggressive/leading-edge, moderate/fast-follower, conservative/risk-averse, or a more specific description supported by context.
Capabilities / constraints
Important skills, infrastructure, data, budget, workflow, policy, or operating constraints.
Risk / consequence context
What failure could mean and how reversible or consequential the application is.
Decision and time horizon
What management is deciding now and over what time period.
Common Agent Output Contract

Each specialist agent should return a structured record that can later be consumed by the team orchestrator. A table, structured form, or JSON-like schema may be used, but the semantic fields should remain consistent across agents.
Output field
Required content
Analytical question
The bounded question this specialist agent answers and the decision it informs.
General ET finding
The best-supported conclusion about the technology itself on this analytical dimension.
Application finding
What the general condition means for the specified application or use case.
Organization-specific finding
What changes because of the organization, industry, adoption posture, capabilities, constraints, and consequence environment.
Evidence
Dated sources, observations, or other evidence that materially support the finding; distinguish evidence from inference.
Confidence and uncertainty
Assumptions, missing evidence, contradictions, confidence, and conditions under which the agent should abstain or qualify its conclusion.
Value / opportunity implication
The most relevant benefit, strategic opportunity, or value condition where the agent's dimension bears on value.
Risk / governance implication
The most relevant risk, control, policy, or human-authority implication where the agent's dimension bears on risk.
Recommendation / management implication
What this specialist perspective implies management should do or consider; keep the recommendation bounded to the agent's expertise.
Change / monitoring triggers
What new evidence, threshold, market signal, organizational change, or passage of time should cause reassessment.
Common Agent Testing Standard
Primary case: Run the agent on the technology, application, and organization supplied for the assignment or selected under instructor guidance.

Context contrast: Run the same emerging technology through a materially different application or organizational context. The output should remain stable where general ET evidence is stable and change where the application or organizational context genuinely matters.

Inspect the difference: Identify one conclusion that appropriately remained the same and one that appropriately changed. If nothing changes, test whether the agent is producing generic analysis rather than contextual judgment.
Preserve failure: Record at least one weak, generic, unsupported, contradictory, or otherwise unsatisfactory output and the revision or control used to improve the agent.
What the Agent Package Must Preserve
Agent name, purpose, and version/date.
Specialist instructions, prompt/workflow configuration, and any bounded code needed to reproduce the agent from the frozen scaffold.
The common input and output contract, including any agent-specific fields.
Evidence/source policy, including how current claims are sourced and how unsupported claims are handled.
Test cases and representative outputs, including the context-contrast test.
Known limitations, abstention conditions, and integration notes for the final team tool.
Frozen Scaffold Package and Reference Toolchain

The instructor distributes one frozen scaffold ZIP through Brightspace: MASY1800_ET_Agent_Scaffold_v1_0.zip. This Brightspace file - not an instructor GitHub repository - is the canonical starting point for Assignments 2-8. Keep the original ZIP unchanged and make a working copy for your own use.

ChatGPT is the required AI environment for the specialist-agent assignments. Use normal ChatGPT for understanding the weekly charge, developing and critiquing specialist reasoning, and interpreting results.
Codex inside ChatGPT is the supported coding/development path for modifying the working scaffold, explaining files, debugging bounded code, and helping run the included local scripts.
Place your working copy in your own GitHub repository and use a branch/commit record appropriate to the assignment. The instructor does not host a GitHub repository for the scaffold.
Do not assume ChatGPT or Codex can always retrieve an arbitrary GitHub link. When necessary, upload the assignment memo and the relevant scaffold files or ZIP directly.

The reference scaffold does not programmatically call the OpenAI API and does not require a separate API account or API key. The included script creates a prompt packet for ChatGPT; you save the returned structured response and validate it locally.
Do not modify files marked FROZEN CORE unless the assignment explicitly authorizes an architectural change. The included integrity checker lets you verify that the common scaffold remains intact.
ChatGPT and Codex Are the Required Working Tools

You are expected to use ChatGPT as the common course AI environment. For Assignments 2-8, Codex is the supported development path for instantiating and modifying the supplied scaffold. ChatGPT/Codex may help you learn unfamiliar material, draft or revise specialist instructions, organize evidence, generate contrast cases, critique classifications, edit bounded code, build structured outputs, and test whether an agent is overgeneralizing. This use of AI is intentional and should make the work faster.

ChatGPT/Codex may generate much of an initial implementation, but that implementation is not by itself evidence of mastery. You remain responsible for specifying the expert behavior, deciding what evidence matters, checking consequential factual claims, recognizing uncertainty, finding deficiencies, improving the agent, and defending the agent design and conclusion you submit.
Use ChatGPT/Codex to accelerate mechanical, exploratory, coding, and drafting work.
Ask ChatGPT to challenge your assumptions, identify contrary evidence, and generate cases that could expose a weak agent.
For current technology status, market adoption, standards, prices, regulation, or other time-sensitive claims, return to the original source and record the date.
Do not treat model memory, an AI-generated summary, or polished prose as evidence by itself.
Be able to explain why your agent reached its conclusion and where its authority should stop.

Submission and Platform Neutrality

Brightspace remains the authoritative location for the frozen scaffold ZIP, weekly assignment memos, due dates, late rules, and semester-specific submission instructions. For Assignments 2-8, students work from a copy of the Brightspace scaffold, use ChatGPT/Codex as the reference development environment, and preserve the working agent in their own GitHub repository with the relevant branch/commit. The Brightspace ZIP remains frozen; student repositories are working copies and evidence of individual development.
Common Top-Level Assessment Rubric
Criterion
Weight
Top-level standard
Professional Task & Deliverable
The assigned professional task was accomplished and the artifact is usable, appropriately bounded, and ready to contribute to the team project.
Evidence & Analysis
Relevant evidence was gathered or produced, consequential claims were checked, and the agent or analysis distinguishes fact, inference, uncertainty, and unsupported assertion.
Contextual Professional Judgment
The student makes a clear, independent, defensible judgment and appropriately distinguishes the general ET state from application-specific and organization-specific implications.
Testing, Verification & Team Handoff
The work includes appropriate testing or verification, preserves limitations or failures, documents material AI use, and provides a usable handoff for the team.

The rubric is intentionally simple: accomplish the professional task, establish credible evidence, make a contextual judgment, and leave behind something the team can reuse. Extra pages, additional agent features, or technical complexity receive no additional credit unless they materially strengthen one of those four elements.
